parts.part: whole site (building complex around the central court)
parts.layout_phase: the 'major construction period' of Buildings I, II, III and probably IV; the radiocarbon list calls the dated level 'Building Level I'
parts.what_was_built: Allahdino is a low silt mound no more than 100 m across. At its highest, central part the excavators cleared an open court about 20 by 8 m with a stone-built well (Well A) and a pavement, surrounded by Buildings I to VII; access to the court was by open passageways between the buildings. Building I, the largest, had two wings joined by 'a platform and drain complex', Building II a stone-lined bathroom with covered drains, Building VII 'a broad brick platform', and two stone-lined drain channels with a movable sluice stone met at the head of the alley between Buildings I and II. Fairservis lists the traits of the complex: every building is partly of stone, 'There is a formality of plan which integrates the structures. There is a general absence of haphazardness both in the way the buildings were constructed and the way they relate one to another', and 'There was no perimeter, or enclosing wall around the site' (pp. 109-110). Stratigraphically, 'there was an early phase when Harappan cattle pastoralists settled the site. This was followed by a major construction period during which Buildings I, II, III and probably IV, were created', with flimsier structures added to the south later (p. 111).
parts.excavator_basis: Not stated in the excavation report, which gives no absolute date and judges from 'The conformity and continuity of artifacts and structures' that the Harappan occupation lasted 'no more than a hundred years at the most' (fairservis1982allahdino p. 111). The range recorded here is the date Fairservis expected when he submitted the two Building Level I samples, 'Date expected to be 1900 +/- 200 BC' (rc-penn-xix p. 215); its basis is not given, and presumably rests on the conventional Harappan chronology of the time.

radiocarbon.context: Charcoal from Bldg Level I, 60cm depth. Date expected to be 1900 +/- 200 BC.
radiocarbon.phase: Building Level I; the only sample Fairservis would associate with the main building period
radiocarbon.curve: MASCA correction factors applied to the 5730-year age (Penn XIX introduction, p. 188, citing Ralph et al. 1973)
radiocarbon.note: Penn XIX gives BP ages on the 5568-year half-life (p. 188); the BC date marked with an asterisk 'has been calculated with the half-life value of 5730 yr and then corrected by means of MASCA correction factors' (p. 188). Fairservis's general comment: 'samples from high on site. Only P-2296 could qualify as assoc with main bldg period; P-2237 and -2295 from last phase of occupation' (p. 214).

syntheses.statement: The Allchins note that at Allahdino 'The main settlement is of the Harappan period and relatively little can be said of the earlier occupation.'

parts.conflicts: The one date Fairservis tied to the main building period, P-2296 (3930 +/- 50 BP), was published with a MASCA-corrected date of 2550 +/- 50 BC, about six centuries older than the 1900 +/- 200 BC he expected; the two samples from the last phase give 2410-2340 and 2180 BC on the same correction, so the dated sequence runs older than his expectation throughout and the spread of the three dates (about 370 years in MASCA terms) is longer than his estimate of a Harappan occupation of at most a hundred years. P-2295-A, from 40 cm in the same 'Building Level I', is 170 radiocarbon years younger than P-2296 at 60 cm.

first_occupation.phase: an early phase in which 'Harappan cattle pastoralists settled the site', identified in Shaffer's sondage in quadrant 5-6, below the major construction period
first_occupation.basis: Stratigraphic only; no date is given for it. Fairservis notes that, contrary to expectation, no Amrian (Early Harappan) material was found in the lower levels (fairservis1982allahdino pp. 109, 111).

notes: Allahdino is a small, unwalled Harappan site near Karachi, and its layout is that of a single planned building complex rather than a town grid: a central court with wells, a paved surface and drains, ringed by buildings with stone footings and platforms that Fairservis describes as integrated by a 'formality of plan'. We include it because the planned complex and its platforms are the layout the brief asks about. The excavator's 1982 summary chapter is our only description of the architecture; the expedition papers (Fairservis 1976 and 1977 on the seals and graffiti, Hoffman and Cleland 1977 on the lithics) and Shaffer's 1974 study 'Allahdino and the Mature Harappan', which holds the stratigraphy, were not available online, nor were Possehl's radiocarbon compilations. The three Pennsylvania dates in Penn XIX are the only determinations we found, and none comes from the early pastoralist phase below the buildings. We found no Bayesian model or later re-dating. The two ways the Penn list states each date (a conventional BP age and a MASCA-corrected BC date) should not be mixed: the BP ages are on the Libby half-life, the BC dates on 5730 years with the MASCA correction.
